title: 2011 AMC 10A Problem 6
statement: Set \(A\) has \(20\) elements, and set \(B\) has \(15\) elements. What is the smallest possible number of elements in \(A \cup B,\) the union of \(A\) and \(B?\)

solutions.text:
To minimize the number of elements in the union, we want to maximize the overlap between the two sets.

We can then assume that \(B\) is contained completely within \(A,\) which means that the union is the same as \(A,\) which has \(20\) elements.

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: The union must contain all elements of the larger set
Make \(B\) a subset of \(A\) to minimize the union
